title: POC scoping - Benchmark harness integration
header:
Date: 2026-10-20T15:00Z
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Sasha Kim (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (Novus CTO), Liam Chen (Novus ML Infra), Priya Singh (Novus SRE), Jordan Patel (Novus Product)
summary: POC scoping focused on benchmark planning and integrating customer's load scripts into Redwood's benchmark harness.
Discussed streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, workload sizing, success criteria (latency p95, throughput, cost), and timelines for a 3-week POC.
topics: Customer scripts and synthetic vs production traces
transcript:
[00:00] Sasha (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya (Novus): Maya here.
[00:08] Liam (Novus): Liam on the call.
[00:10] Priya (Novus): Priya here.
[00:12] Jordan (Novus): Jordan.
[00:15] Sasha (Redwood): Cool, I'll hand over to Ethan to frame the benchmark plan and how we plug in your scripts.
[00:22] Ethan (Redwood): Thanks. So goal today is to scope the POC: what scripts you have, the target load, and the success metrics. We'll run Redwood's benchmark harness in your staging VPC; you can either supply sample production traces or we can generate synthetic traffic that matches your distribution.
[00:35] Maya: Quick thing — we want to validate both streaming use cases (partial token streaming for chat) and non-streaming batch endpoints (for doc summarization). They'll behave differently, so want to see both.
[00:45] Ethan: Absolutely, streaming will exercise smaller per-request byte increments and longer-lived connections; non-streaming will be more request/response oriented and stresses throughput. For streaming we measure first-byte latency and per-token latency; for non-streaming we measure end-to-end p95.
[01:02] Liam: For context, our current stack does embeddings and chat. We're on k8s in AWS, and have a managed model infra team. We get about 40 concurrent chat sessions at peak, average 3-4 turns per session. That roughly maps to 120 requests/minute, but some bursts up to 300 req/min.
[01:20] Ethan: Good, we'll size the harness to emulate burst windows. For the POC what throughput do you want validated?
[01:25] Maya: We want to see 50 req/s sustained and ability to handle 150 req/s burst for short periods without tail-latency spikes.
[01:34] Sasha: Noted. Any cost targets or acceptable latency SLOs?
[01:38] Priya: Latency target p95 under 300ms for non-streaming, for chat streaming first-byte under 150ms ideally. Cost: we're tracking per-token cost but open to recommendations.
[01:48] Ethan: We'll capture token counts in the harness so you get per-request and per-token metrics.
[01:52] Jordan: About scripts: we have a set of python-based load scripts built on locust and a small wrapper that replays production traces anonymized. Are those compatible with your harness?
[02:02] Ethan: Yes, we can ingest locust scripts or provide a shim. Two options: 1) you drop your scripts in a repo we mount into the harness runner in your staging VPC; 2) we provide our harness templates and you port the request generators. Mounting repo is faster for POC.
[02:17] Liam: Mounting is preferred. Timeline wise we can get that repo ready in 2-3 days.
[02:22] Ethan: Great. We'll need a small runner VM or container in your staging VPC with network egress to Redwood's harness control plane, plus IAM role for S3 access if you want to push logs.
[02:33] Priya: We'll need an architecture diagram and least-privilege permissions. Also SOC2 concerns — will this POC require any special audit?
[02:41] Sasha: We'll share our security pack — SSO options, KMS usage, audit logs. For the POC we run in your staging; data is ephemeral and can be configured to not persist. We'll include our SOC2 summary and a whitepaper.
[02:53] Maya: Good. Back to metrics: Besides p95 and throughput, we want error rate, percent of time above SLO, cost per 1k tokens, and tail-latency (p99).
[03:04] Ethan: We'll surface those in the harness dashboard. Also track memory and GPU utilization per host, KV cache hit rates if you use caching, and queue lengths for batching.
[03:15] Liam: On the subject of model variants — we run a few models: a 7B chat model quantized, and a larger 13B model for longer context. Can the harness switch between variants to compare?
[03:24] Ethan: Yes, harness supports multiple model configs and kernels. We'll run back-to-back runs: baseline (your current model+quant), and Redwood-optimized execution path. We may recommend quantization changes but POC will focus on serving performance not model accuracy changes.
[03:38] Jordan: For the streaming tests are you going to measure partial output latency per token and also costs?
[03:44] Ethan: Yes, we measure per-token latency and aggregate. Streaming often increases connection overhead but reduces time-to-first-sensible-token. The harness will approximate real-world framing and net chunk sizes.
[03:55] Priya: Any limits on concurrent connections to the harness? We need to repro thousands of open websockets in our load test later.
[04:03] Ethan: We can simulate large concurrency but will need to size the runner and possibly use distributed clients. For the POC we'll scope up to 1k concurrent connections if required; for larger, we recommend a follow-on stress test.
[04:16] Maya: OK, what's the proposed POC timeline?
[04:19] Sasha: We think a three-week POC: week 0 (prep) — repo and harness access, week 1 run baseline tests, week 2 tuning and follow-up runs, with final report at end of week 3. If Novus can get scripts in 3 days we can start next week.
[04:34] Liam: That aligns with our rollout calendar. We aim to decide by end of November.
[04:39] Ethan: Success criteria recap: non-streaming p95 <300ms, streaming first-byte <150ms, sustain 50 req/s and handle 150 req/s bursts, error rate <0.5%, and cost per 1k tokens below your current baseline.
[04:55] Maya: Also want to include integration tests for RBAC and audit logging; if those fail POC isn't a pass.
[05:03] Sasha: Noted — we'll add security checks to the checklist.
[05:07] Jordan: Small nit — network egress will be proxied, will that break streaming websockets?
[05:12] Ethan: We may need to test proxy settings; websockets generally work with standard proxy but we'll provide docs. If not, we can do tunnel-based runner.
[05:20] Priya: Do you collect raw transcripts? We need to ensure PII redaction.
[05:25] Sasha: We don't persist raw PII by default; the harness can be configured to redact or not store transcripts. We'll provide config options.
[05:33] Maya: Great. For the benchmarks, can you share sample dashboards and the CSV outputs so we ingest into our monitoring?
[05:39] Ethan: Yes — dashboard links, raw CSVs, and a JSON report per run. We'll push artifacts to an S3 bucket you control.
[05:46] Liam: Regarding cost calculations, do you estimate token counts or actual tokens from runs?
[05:50] Ethan: Both — harness logs actual token counts per request and we can model cost using Redwood pricing or your internal cost model.
[05:58] Jordan: Any blockers on our side right now?
[06:01] Ethan: Just the repo with scripts and a staging runner. Also confirm which models/configs to test and whether you want GPU profiling.
[06:10] Maya: We'll provide the repo and the model list by Friday (2026-10-23).
[06:14] Sasha: Great. We'll book the initial harness window for the week of 2026-10-27.
[06:19] Ethan: One more note — streaming fragmentation sizes and chunk intervals can materially affect cost; we'll include a small experiment to show tradeoffs.
[06:28] Priya: Sounds good.
[06:30] Sasha: Ok quick recap of action items and who owns what...
[06:34] "Sasha (Redwood): Sasha to share benchmark harness repo link and security docs.
[06:38] "Ethan (Redwood): Ethan to prepare load test config templates and example locust shim, plus initial model config matrix.
[06:44] "Maya (Novus): Maya/Liam to drop the repo and sample production traces by 2026-10-23.
[06:50] "Priya (Novus): Priya to provision a staging runner container and open egress to Redwood testing endpoint, or confirm tunneling approach.
[06:58] "Jordan (Novus): Jordan to validate audit/logging requirements and share with Sasha.
[07:03] Sasha (Redwood): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the first run and the security pack.
[07:09] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:12] End of recording.
